questions.stem: Why is the reaction between ethene and bromine described as an addition reaction?

options.text: Because heat must be added to start the reaction
Because the double bond opens up and atoms add to both carbons, forming only one product
Because two molecules of ethene are added together
Because bromine is added as a catalyst

questions.explanation: In an addition reaction, the C=C double bond breaks open and the atoms of the other reactant (in this case Br2) add to the two carbon atoms. Only one product is formed (1,2-dibromoethane) and no atoms are lost. This is characteristic of all addition reactions.
